Query-conditioned fusion relevance must causally control how views contribute to the latent fabric; reliability alone is not relevance.
Final public judgment gradient must reach the fusion route scorer through the latent path.
Merely available irrelevant views are not compulsory latent recoverability targets.
Padded structured fields and arbitrary hidden values behind their masks cannot alter valid field states or pooled context.
Ordered execution must consume the relation semantic state for the current operator step; averaging relation semantic states across the program may not own executable edge meaning.

Holding evidence, direction, traversal and learned readout preference fixed, changing only ROLE_SOURCE versus ROLE_TARGET must causally switch the executor structural endpoint readout and final relational probability.
Graph source/target views can activate only from relation probability mass represented by valid runtime edges; duplicate edges may not inflate that mass.
Whole-program relation state must be aggregated using actual survival-weighted relation assignment mass, while exact step-conditioned relation states remain preserved.
Shared query/schema interaction must expose masked token-local evidence on both query and schema sides for relations, global factors, and step-conditioned factors.
Schema-token grounding loss must keep a live gradient path into shared query/backbone semantics.
Query/schema evidence surfaces share the existing token-grounding macro budget so adding banks cannot silently dominate optimization.
Partial schema-evidence supervision inputs fail closed.
Synthetic operator rows must materialize exact query, relation-schema, factor-schema, and step-factor-schema evidence spans and pass split/leakage audit.
Type-incompatible relation edges are exactly excluded before continuous graph propagation and cannot contaminate structured/evidence state before Binder.
Binder null support must prevent graph source/target summaries from entering final fusion even when a soft pre-Binder graph was active.

Binder sparse support must represent structurally/semantically relevant candidate support and remain neutral to reliability/recency arbitration so one global support set cannot violate later step-local modifier semantics.

Reliability, recency, temporal, and provenance edge scalars must be neutralized before executor edge-state construction whenever the corresponding semantic modifier is OFF, while ON retains sensitivity.

Global graph and evidence-specialist views must keep explicit reliability/recency/temporal/provenance criterion channels neutral because one global view cannot represent conflicting step-local ON/OFF semantics; raw criterion values remain available to the step-conditioned Executor.
A candidate marked invalid by candidate_valid_mask is structurally impossible and may never outrank a valid candidate regardless of learned logit magnitude.
Padded candidates must be exactly excluded from public-judgment normalization and gradients; with one valid candidate the classification loss is exactly zero regardless of padded logits.

When a causal behavioral lane is inactive, exact padded-candidate exclusion may not create -inf×0/NaN zero losses; zero-return paths must depend only on valid logits and padded candidates must receive exactly zero gradient.
Structural masks must preserve probability mass on valid entries even when valid learned logits are far below legacy finite sentinels; explicitly permitted empty slices must return exact zero mass.
An inactive semantic relation/factor candidate may never receive probability or erase an active candidate merely because learned active logits cross a finite masking sentinel.
An unavailable runtime view may never receive fusion mass or erase available-view mass when learned route logits take extreme finite values.

When one relation is reused across steps and reliability is ON for an earlier step but OFF for a later step, Binder's global sparse support may not let the earlier criterion alter the later step's edge eligibility.
A mixed-step program with reliability ON then OFF must not let a global graph/evidence view apply the global criterion to both steps; explicit global criterion channels remain neutral.

Additional runtime views, descriptors, availability, and reliability may be permuted together without changing fused state, latent pooled state, or public judgment; runtime view position is not a hidden semantic identity axis.
Runtime candidate ordering is not semantic: jointly permuting candidate states and masks must only permute candidate logits, with no candidate-position identity parameter or bias.

Role, traversal and control remain deliberate whole-program executable semantics while direction and evidence modifiers are step-local. Step-factor semantic context may include every runtime bank, but copied role/traversal/control step labels must not silently create unsupported structural opcodes.

Candidate text is comparison material rather than an independent policy: when the governed latent judgment signal is removed, distinct candidate content may not create candidate-specific ranking logits. Every candidate-specific final-readout feature must contain latent interaction.

Binder supervision must encode query-relevant structural/semantic support, not relation-key equality. Same-relation irrelevant edges remain hard negatives, while query-relevant reliability/recency/temporal/provenance alternatives survive Binder for step-local Executor arbitration.

The current full-envelope successor must have an executable pre-gradient shortcut audit registered in CI for every shortcut probe declared by the semantic/operator curriculum contract. Superseded T2 shortcut receipts cannot satisfy this obligation.

Residual CONTINUE survival after the final available reasoning slot is truncation, not successful relational completion. A truncated program may not activate graph/evidence relational views; global semantic relational activity must require completion just as Executor confidence does.

Before gradient, the full-envelope successor must define its own sealed final-v2 package builder/auditor/freezer and evaluator contract targeting N0FullEnvelopeTrainableSystemV1. Legacy final-self-validation v1/v3 artifacts may not satisfy or be promoted into successor final-v2 authority.

Relational completion must use the exact joint survival/event mass. Marginal P(program starts) multiplied by marginal P(not truncated/unknown) may not fabricate graph/evidence activity when start and completion occur on disjoint branches.
Executor confidence must be zero when no probability mass both starts a relational program and subsequently reaches STOP, even if P(start)>0 and P(not truncated)>0 separately.

Global relation semantics for an asserted completed program must be conditioned on branches that later reach STOP. Relation distributions from branches that only continue to UNKNOWN/truncation may not contaminate the completed graph/evidence program summary.

Executor path state used for completed relational output must be conditioned on successful future STOP completion. Relation steps that exist only on branches ending in truncation/UNKNOWN may not move the completed-program frontier.

CPU smoke coverage or FINAL-only long rows cannot satisfy this training-curriculum obligation.
The behavioral row-to-system compiler must carry governed runtime internal-view descriptor text from curriculum rows instead of forcing only the short built-in descriptor wording.

Before gradient, materialize and audit public TRAIN/DEV long-context rows covering every governed text surface with unchanged targets, decisive semantic content beyond the native-window operating point, no FINAL rows, and no private identity data.

Each behavioral row must own independent runtime relation-candidate objects so downstream surface interventions cannot mutate the canonical public relation bank or contaminate later TRAIN/DEV/FINAL materialization.

Long additional runtime-view source and descriptor text must compile into the same optimizer-facing source-text and descriptor-text inputs consumed by N0FullEnvelopeTrainableSystemV1, crossing the native-window operating point without a fixed view taxonomy.

The DEV stage-gate evaluator must fail closed on missing scalar metrics, require exact-source static proof obligations for source-invariant gates, and never infer a pass from an incomplete registry.

Behavioral DEV must actually instantiate candidate-answer cardinality and reasoning-depth points beyond TRAIN while the sealed FINAL remains beyond DEV. Reasoning-depth extrapolation rows must use distinct chain entities and distinct public answer candidates. Increasing DEV/FINAL path length may not create label ambiguity through deterministic entity-index aliasing.

J3 DEV must explicitly measure that labeled relevant/recoverable source views are represented by at least one latent slot across the base behavioral fabric, heterogeneous runtime-view supplement, and long-context supplement. Negative proof that irrelevant available views are not forced recoverable does not satisfy the positive recoverability gate required by final-v2.

J3 DEV checkpoint selection must explicitly gate candidate-dependent invariance to removal of labeled irrelevant evidence across base behavioral, heterogeneous runtime-view, and long-context lanes. Static proof that irrelevant available views are not recoverability targets does not establish learned judgment invariance.

DEV checkpoint selection must evaluate the exact TRAIN/DEV artifacts hash-bound into the candidate's pre-gradient public-mixture manifest, including the natural-relation bank and governed teacher registry/audit. File substitution after training is forbidden.

Subset-derived DEV metrics may not pass vacuously when their evaluated subset is empty. Empirical gate specs can bind an explicit coverage metric and minimum count, and all registered subset gates must use it.

The required plurality intervention must supervise at least two co-valid runtime relation hypotheses and nonzero calibrated uncertainty. A row that says 'preserve both' in text while still training one hard relation target with zero uncertainty is not plurality supervision.

Multi-positive relation supervision must optimize a normalized soft target over all co-valid runtime hypotheses rather than combining it with hard representative cross-entropy that would reintroduce forced top-1 semantics.

J1 DEV checkpoint selection must measure mass preserved on the co-valid relation set, forced-top1 collapse rate, and calibrated plurality uncertainty. Plurality rows must not be included in the hard representative relation-sequence exact gate, because that would select checkpoints that undo the multi-hypothesis training objective.
The DEV plurality primitive must score probability mass over all co-valid hypotheses and distinguish collapse onto one valid hypothesis from genuine multi-hypothesis preservation.

A plurality curriculum row must survive the real semantic-operator batch compiler and reach optimizer-facing multi-positive relation targets. Builder-only plurality fields do not count if batch compilation crashes or drops them.

The decisive-evidence counterfactual must supervise an increase in normalized public-judgment uncertainty, not merely a decrease in target probability. Becoming confidently wrong after removing decisive evidence cannot satisfy the uncertainty gate.

J3 DEV checkpoint selection must measure at least 0.05 normalized public-judgment entropy increase after decisive evidence removal across base behavioral, heterogeneous runtime-view, and long-context lanes, with nonempty coverage.

Before gradient, DEV must exercise a factor-cardinality point beyond TRAIN but below sealed FINAL, a distinct runtime type-schema surface, a distinct public domain surface, and a held-out modifier combination different from the sealed FINAL recency+provenance combination.

J3 checkpoint selection must empirically gate factor-cardinality extrapolation, non-FINAL factor-combination transfer, unseen type-schema transfer, and public domain transfer with nonempty coverage before FINAL remains sealed.

Before gradient, FINAL-v2 must have an executable evaluator and complete gate registry for every precommitted final-contract gate. Both implementation and gate mapping must be hash-bound into the frozen package so they cannot be authored or changed after candidate FINAL results are observed.

The sealed successor FINAL-v2 package must contain an independent synthetic semantic-operator component with relation families absent from TRAIN/DEV and explicit plurality, source/target, ordered, mixed-step, unknown/defer, and evidence-grounding cases. Behavioral FINAL plus natural FewRel alone cannot satisfy the separate synthetic heldout-operator gates.

The public semantic-operator row builder must support a sealed FINAL authority mode with caller-owned heldout relation/entity pools while preserving TRAIN/DEV defaults. FINAL rows must be training- and model-selection-ineligible and explicitly final-only.

The sealed FINAL-v2 package must include heterogeneous runtime-described view challenges and cross-native-window long-context challenges on every governed text surface. TRAIN/DEV runtime-view/long-context coverage or short behavioral FINAL rows cannot satisfy these FINAL closure gates.
FINAL runtime-view and long-context generators reuse the registered runtime-shaped interfaces in sealed FINAL authority mode rather than substituting TRAIN/DEV rows or a fixed view/context taxonomy.

A hand-authored boolean opening JSON or a DEV receipt from another candidate may not authorize FINAL.

Passing tokenizer stress or long-context token alignment alone may not substitute for P40A.

Every optimizer-facing successor data artifact must hash-match the exact audited full public-mixture manifest at training time, including semantic, semantic-long, behavioral, runtime-view, long-context, natural rows/bank, broad replay source/corpus receipt, and governed teacher registry/audit. Arbitrary CLI substitutions are forbidden.

The staged trainer must bind the passed tokenizer stress receipt to the exact tokenizer.json and public corpus receipt registered by the audited public mixture. A generic PASS tokenizer audit cannot authorize a different tokenizer or corpus.

P42 CPU and P43 GPU receipts must hash-bind the exact registered topology, qualification contract, semantic config/checkpoint, governed tokenizer, public source/corpus receipt, and for GPU the exact audited mixture. Same-status receipts from other artifacts cannot authorize gradient.

The P43 GPU no-gradient memory dry run must exercise row/bank artifacts that hash-match every optimizer-facing lane in the audited full public mixture, including broad replay and governed teacher provenance. Memory routing may not be chosen from substituted easier data.

Gradient authorization must be achievable without editing the exact source revision after P40/P40A/P40B/P40C/P42/P43/P39PN receipts are produced. A governed runtime authorizer must revalidate the exact public corpus and teacher bank, bind every optimizer-facing artifact and runtime receipt, keep FINAL closed, and emit the sole optimizer/gradient/GPU-training authorization consumed by the trainer.

The staged trainer must support exact-state same-stage continuation beyond an invocation's optimizer-step operating point. J1 may not become non-resumable, J2/J3 continuation may not be confused with a predecessor stage transition, and an arbitrary max-optimizer-steps value may not become an implicit stage-completion or capability ceiling.

The precommitted 'first checkpoint satisfying every active DEV gate' rule must be executable rather than advisory. Stage checkpoints must form a hash-linked same-stage chain, every chain member through the selected candidate must have an exact DEV receipt, earlier passing candidates must block later selection, and J2/J3 transition plus FINAL opening must consume the resulting first-pass selection receipt.

J1->J2 and J2->J3 must load the exact first-DEV-selected predecessor model plus preserved objective-balancer state, while restarting AdamW and the stage-local warmup/cosine scheduler. A predecessor scheduler that may already be deeply decayed or at zero learning rate may not silently govern newly activated stage owners.

Every J2/J3 checkpoint, including same-stage descendants, must retain the exact predecessor checkpoint, DEV evaluation, and first-pass selection receipt hashes that authorized entry into the stage. Successful transition authority may not disappear from descendant checkpoint provenance.

The precommitted scheduler horizon is an optimization operating point, not stage completion. Its decay must retain a strictly positive precommitted learning-rate floor so same-stage continuation after the nominal horizon can still update weights until DEV determines saturation; a zero-LR tail may not silently convert the horizon into a capability ceiling.
